result.rationale: In parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts, the schema uses computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()]. ZodString does not override toString, so both keys are literally the string "[object Object]"; the second entry overwrites the first, leaving a schema that effectively only requires access_token. The comment in the diff ('Assume that any property with a number is the expiry') shows the intended validation, and the mechanism described (undefined expiry stored, tokens treated as expired) follows from the visible code paths in CalendarService.ts that read token.expiry_dat

judged_text: Both computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] evaluate to the string "[object Object]" (ZodString does not override toString), so the second entry overwrites the first and the "minimum" schema requires only access_token — the intended "any property with a number is the expiry" validation does not exist. Sharing mode accepts token responses with no expiry field at all, so callers store undefined expiry_date/expires_in into credentials; tokens are then treated as expired on every use (or mis-handled per app), and the documented validation invariant of the feature is never enforced.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` defines computed object keys using `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Here `z.string()` is a Zod schema object, and `.toString()` is evaluated immediately to a string key (not a Zod “pattern key”); both expressions will stringify to the same constant (e.g. "[object Object]") and the latter overwrites the former. As a result, the schema does not enforce “any property with a number is the expiry” and in sharing mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`) token responses can pass validation without any expiry field, matching the finding’s claim that the intended invariant is not enforced.
